title: Uniform moment bounds control the essential supremum
statement: Let $(A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f:A\to\mathbb R$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable. For $C\in[0,\infty]$ and $N\in\mathbb N$, suppose that $\|f\|_{L^n(\mu)}\le C$ for every natural number $n\ge N$. Then $\|f\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}\le C$.
hypotheses_covered: $f:A\to\mathbb R$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable
For every $n\in\mathbb N$ with $N\le n$, the extended $L^n$ seminorm of $f$ is at most $C$
replaced: Let $f$ be an almost everywhere strongly measurable real function on an arbitrary measure space $(A,\mu)$, let $C\in[0,\infty]$ and $N\in\mathbb N$. If $\|f\|_n\le C$ for every integer $n\ge N$, then $\|f\|_\infty\le C$.
